Now they are dying: in the Grizzly Hills the Scourge spreads disease through their ziggurats and raises their dead, bounty hunters sell them alive to the armies, and even the spirits of their ancestors find no rest.
hint: Learned among the dying ice trolls.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.

parts.body: In Zul'Drak, their heartland, the Drakkari slay their own animal gods at their altars so that their prophets may drink the gods' power against the Scourge.

title: The Zandalari
body: The Zandalari are an ancient tribe of troll priests and scholars from the isle of Zandalar, honored by the other troll nations. In Zul'Drak they have come to defend the gods the Drakkari are slaying, holding a refuge at Zim'Torga, and they warn that the power the Drakkari win by killing their gods is fleeting and will be lost to them for all eternity.

parts.body: Their chronicler records the end of the empire: the Drakkari were exiled from the other troll nations for their extreme violence, and Northrend was once the far north of Kalimdor before the Sundering.

hint: Learned among the troll priests who came to save the gods.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.

title: The Wolvar
body: The wolvar are wolf-like hunters of Northrend who live in tribes. The Rageclaw of Zul'Drak lived beside the Drakkari as allies for thousands of years until the trolls turned on them; the Snowfall Glade tribe raids the tuskarr of the Dragonblight; and the Frenzyheart, newcomers to Sholazar Basin, mean to take it from the gorlocs.
hint: Learned among the wolf-folk of the north.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.

title: The Oracles
body: The Oracles are the gorlocs of Sholazar Basin, a gentle, chattering people who call outsiders dryskins and believe the Great Ones made them. They tend the stone shrines they think the Great Ones left behind, rain, mist, lightning and moss, feeding them with shinies dug from the earth, and the wolvar of the Frenzyheart war on them for the land.
hint: Learned among the gorlocs who tend the great stones.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.

title: The Sons of Hodir
body: The Sons of Hodir are the frost giants of Dun Niffelem in the Storm Peaks, who look to the keeper Hodir for protection and guidance and treasure everfrost, ice that never melts, as the symbol of their people's heart. Once allies of Thorim, they have nursed a hatred of the Stormlord since a dark day at Thunderfall, and they war with the Hyldnir of Brunnhildar. Outsiders earn their regard slowly, by deeds.
hint: Learned among the frost giants of the peaks.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.

title: The Earthen
body: The earthen are dwarves of living stone, shaped by the titans to build and tend their works. Loken expelled those of Ulduar, and since then the weakest have died and the strongest craftsmen have been reborn as warriors, holding out at Bouldercrag's Refuge and on the Terrace of the Makers against the iron dwarves. In the Grizzly Hills earthen and stone giants besiege the iron dwarves at Thor Modan.
hint: Learned among the stone-born exiles of Ulduar.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.

title: The Silver Covenant
body: The Silver Covenant is the order of high elves who rejected the admission of blood elves into the Kirin Tor, gathered by Ranger General Vereesa Windrunner and joined to the Alliance in Northrend. In Dalaran they keep the Silver Enclave, whose guardian mages teleport out any member of the Horde who tries to enter, and in Crystalsong Forest they hold Windrunner's Overlook, facing the Sunreavers across the ruins.
hint: Learned among the high elves who stood apart.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.

title: The Sunreavers
body: The Sunreavers are the blood elves who follow Archmage Aethas Sunreaver, through whose efforts the Horde was accepted into Dalaran at all. They keep Sunreaver's Sanctuary, whose guardian mages teleport away any member of the Alliance who strays inside, and in Crystalsong Forest they hold Sunreaver's Command, facing the Silver Covenant across the ruins.
hint: Learned among the blood elves of the Kirin Tor.
notes: Rewritten 2026-10-25 for the reorganization pilot: shorter, context first.
